summary:
Podlaskie saw Poland's most violent assault on a public LGBTQ event: at the 20 July 2019 Białystok Equality March, roughly 1,000 marchers were attacked by thousands of far-right and football-hooligan groups who attempted to block the route. Police detained 25 people; 32 counter-demonstrations had been registered that day, including a prayer vigil at the Cathedral Basilica. In the run-up, Archbishop Tadeusz Wojda had a proclamation read in every church across the region. The surrounding Białystok County had been declared an LGBT-free zone in 2019, though the city itself did not adopt one, and its mayor questioned whether the march was "needed" while the PiS city council filed a motion to stop it.

The state's protective response improved materially: at the fourth Equality March (28 September 2024), ~300 participants were escorted by 500 police officers and the Podlaskie police reported zero incidents. This is positive evidence under the single-incident rule (institutional learning, proportionate deployment), but it does not erase the 2019 pattern—organised mass violence met with a partial 25-person detention response, embedded in a documented church-and-county mobilisation infrastructure.

Score of 0.44 sits 0.08 below the national 0.52. Slightly above Subcarpathian (0.42), which lacked Podlaskie's demonstrable five-year improvement in state protection, but below Masovian (0.56), where the institutional machinery runs the other way.

Encyclopedia article on the Bialystok Equality March: Podlaskie described as Poland's 'bible belt' and a governing-party stronghold; the surrounding Bialystok County had been declared an LGBT-free zone in 2019 while the city's independent mayor allowed the march despite criticism; on 7 July 2019 the Catholic archbishop had a proclamation calling the march 'blasphemy against God' read in all churches across the voivodeship; approximately a thousand marchers were opposed by thousands of far-right and ultra football fans who attacked them, with solidarity events following.

Regional news report (28 September 2024): about 300 people took part in the fourth Bialystok Equality March under the slogan 'to live without fear', protected by 500 police officers; counter-demonstrations formed at several points on the route but the voivodeship police reported no incidents after the march - organisers stressed showing LGBT+ people as part of the local community.
